title: Speaking in Tongues: The Weight of Translation in Writing Classrooms
author: Yu, Terry
summary: Yu explores translation as a core concept for writing and reading instruction. He distinguishes between narrow code-based views of translation and broader interpretive understandings, then applies translation theory to classroom practice. The piece demonstrates how students can use AI prompts as translation briefs, examining how specified intentions, audiences, and purposes shape linguistic choices. Three historical examples (Emancipation Proclamation messages for enslaved families, Union soldiers, and British Parliament) show how Nord's concept of loyalty in translation reveals power dynamics in language use.
points: Translation briefs specify what a target text needs to do and accomplish, not just what it says
Using AI to fulfill translation briefs makes visible the relationship between purpose, audience, and linguistic choice
Students learn that language always involves choices about loyalty to different audiences and intentions
quotes: A translation brief is the set of instructions that tells the translator what the translation needs to do, not what it needs to say, but what it needs to accomplish.

Loyalty removes the translator's obligation to text fidelity between linguistic systems and strengthens a duty to privilege the intentions of the author and the outcome for the target.” Archived from Terry Yu Substack on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
